name: Eventual Consistency (basic)
description: Basic eventual consistency for replicated data stores, defined axiomatically over abstract executions with visibility and arbitration relations (in analogy to weak shared-memory models) by two axioms: EVENTUAL guarantees an update cannot stay invisible to infinitely many operations on the same object, so if updates stop replicas converge to the same state; THINAIR forbids out-of-thin-air values. Causal (and further sequential/linearizable) consistency are obtained by adding successively stronger ordering axioms (POCV/POCA, then COCV/COCA) on top of it, so eventual consistency is strictly weaker than causal consistency — the causal consistency of Burckhardt's framework, i.e. causal convergence (CCv), reached here via per-object causal. First given a formal definition in MSR-TR-2013-39 (2013).

catSupport.note: Eventual delivery is a liveness property over infinite executions ('all but finitely many operations see a given write'). cat checks safety conditions on one finite candidate execution and has no way to state it.
